D1.question: what share of a 1.84 km map cell can be ploughed, given the slope the map resolves?
D1.rule_kept: the GAEZ terrain-slope rule the tier constants already encode (Fischer et al. 2012, GAEZ v3/v4 slope classes on 90 m SRTM): land under 8 % slope fully arable, 8-16 % 0.6, 16-30 % 0.3, steeper 0.05
D1.earth_target: for every ~1.85 km Earth cell, the GAEZ rule applied to the share of its 90 m pixels in each slope class (Copernicus GLO-90 DEM, 3 arc-seconds, open data); sea and flat water (elevation <= 0, or exactly flat over > 50 % of the cell) excluded
D1.predictors: what the map has at its own resolution: slope of the ~1.85 km block-mean surface (central differences, degrees), and the block-mean elevation

candidates.baseline: today's rule: ARABLE_BY_TIER by the map's tier tops applied to the block-mean elevation (62 / 814 / 1135 / 2528 m)
candidates.S: a(S) = lo + (hi - lo) / (1 + (S / S0)^k), fitted (lo, hi, S0, k) by least squares on development cells
candidates.S_band: a(S) as above with hi set per elevation band (lowland / upland) - adopted over S only if it lowers development RMSE by >= 0.01

tiles.why: old-world farming land of c. AD 200 and its margins, each set mixing plains, hills and mountains; none has been used for any fit

D1.blind_gate: on the blind tiles, the chosen candidate's RMSE against the Earth target is below the baseline's in at least 8 of 12 tiles and in total, and its mean bias is within +/- 0.05
D1.map_check: the map's own 1.84 km slope distribution in tier 1 is compared with Earth lowland slopes at the same scale (output/terrain_erosion_20261107/earth_lowland_slopes.json ref2) and reported, since a(S) is applied to the map's slopes
D1.if_it_passes: harvest/export.py geometry takes the arable share from a(S) on the atlas's terrain file (tier constants stay for atlases without one); the farming, population, settlement and control layers inherit it at the next release
D1.if_it_fails: the tier constants stay and the result is reported

result.weak_spots: over-estimates arable land in finely dissected hill country whose 1.85 km slope is moderate (Shanxi loess +0.19, Fujian hills +0.20)
result.map_check: map slopes vs Earth cells in the same absolute elevation band: tiers 3-4 match (arable 0.44 / 0.30 vs Earth 0.47 / 0.29); tiers 1-2 are steeper than Earth land at 0-62 m / 62-814 m, but the tiers are relative bands (tier 1 = the lowest 70 % of land), so the band comparison is indicative only; output/terrain_erosion_20261107/earth_lowland_slopes.json ref2 was not used because its scale is undocumented
result.map_effect: land-weighted arable share 0.744 -> 0.739; per tier 0.85 / 0.58 / 0.44 / 0.30 (constants 0.85 / 0.75 / 0.45 / 0.08); tier-1 valley floors 0.91
result.wired: harvest/export.py geometry (atlases with a terrain file, recorded in atlas.json world.terrain_file by rotclimate/atlas.py); data/arable_slope_model.json; takes effect at the next release

D1b.status: frozen before the Earth harness is rebuilt
D1b.why: the arable share feeds farm capacity, people, towns and control on Earth too; the Earth harness (scripts/land_people_earth.py, 5 arc-min WorldClim) still takes it from relief tiers, and FALLOW = 0.68 was fitted on that rule (North China Plain AD 2 census at capacity). A map on D1 and an Earth harness on relief tiers would no longer be one calibrated chain.
change: Earth harness arable = mean of a(S) (D1 parameters) over each 5 arc-min cell, S from ETOPO 2022 60 arc-second slopes (the ~1.85 km scale a(S) was fitted at), land where ETOPO > 0
FALLOW refitted by the same rule as before: North China Plain capacity = its AD 2 census density (80.7 per km2)

checks.control: the Earth control development pools (Rome AD 150, Han AD 2), v2.1 rules without ruggedness (beta 0 of geography_control_a2): balanced accuracy before (0.849 / 0.664) and after, the whole Earth chain rebuilt in a separate worktree (harness, windows, food fields, staffing chain, territory)

gates.population_no_harm: RMS not worse by more than 0.05
gates.control_no_harm: each pool loses no more than 0.01 balanced accuracy

D2.status: frozen before the Earth irrigation data are downloaded
D2.question: which land near a river can be irrigated? Today: exp(-d/6 km) from navigable rivers and 0.6 exp(-d/2.5 km) from streams, by distance only, so a slope 300 m above its river counts as much as the floodplain beside it
D2.earth_reference: Historical Irrigation Dataset (Siebert et al. 2015, HESS 19, 1521-1545; CC0; doi:10.13019/M20599): area equipped for irrigation in 1900 at 5 arc-min, the authors' main (HYDE-based) estimate, as a fraction of cell area. 1900 is before pumped irrigation spread, so it shows where river water reaches fields by gravity, not how much was irrigated c. AD 200

candidates.baseline: the distance rule above (Natural Earth 10 m rivers, as in scripts/land_people_earth.py)
candidates.hand: distance rule x exp(-max(H, 0) / H0), H = height of the ~1.85 km cell above its nearest river cell (ETOPO 2022 60 arc-second), averaged to 5 arc-min; H0 in (10, 20, 40, 80, 160) m

D2.cells: land cells of the Earth harness window (0-56 N, 12 W-125 E) with annual P / PET < 0.65 (where irrigation decides farming), within 30 km of a mapped river

split.blind: 60 E - 125 E (South, Central and East Asia)

D2.metric: AUC of the candidate score for cells with >= 10 % of their area equipped for irrigation in 1900 against the rest
D2.selection: H0 with the best development AUC
D2.blind_gate: blind AUC of the chosen H0 above the baseline by >= 0.01
D2.if_it_passes: the map: irrigation x exp(-H / H0) with H above the nearest drawn river on height map v2.1; the Earth harness the same; FALLOW refitted and the D1b no-harm checks repeated (regional populations, control dev pools) before any release

result.hid_product: AEI_HYDE_FINAL_IR_1900 (CP variant reported as sensitivity: same ranking)
result.note: H0 = 10 m is the smallest value of the frozen grid (best on development and blind alike); a narrower gate was not tested
result.next: apply to the map and the Earth harness, refit FALLOW and repeat the D1b no-harm checks before the (combined D1 + D2) release; the D1-only release was stopped before any stage finished

checks_d1_plus_d2.weak_spot: Egypt ln(hist/cap) +0.32 -> +0.64: the gate removes desert cliffs within 6 km of the Nile; the 6 km distance decay is narrower than the 10-20 km floodplain (older limitation)
